assumptions.chosen: Exactly as the recorded decision record and its owner summary already define it: the count n is the number of residual items in the decision record recorded for that acceptance decision (the decision-record artifact the decision references) whose kind is not "should" (unverified should-criteria) and not "advisory_constraint" (advisory constraints); "Nothing is accepted without proof" is shown when n is 0 (the record's attention is "clean"). This matches the wording "N item(s) would be accepted without proof" / "Nothing is accepted without proof" of the explanation the control loop already writes for the same decision. The text is "1 item would be accepted without proof" for n = 1 and "{n} items would be accepted without proof" for n >= 2.

assumptions.chosen: Like the other preview demo data (APP_ENV=preview only, idempotent, also on a preview database seeded earlier), the Demo Project gains two demo tasks in state DONE, each with one open acceptance decision whose recorded context references a stored decision-record artifact: T4 "Demo: share a list", whose recorded decision record has attention "review" and three residual items - two counted ones (kinds such as "finding" and "verifier") and one of kind "should" - so the page shows "2 items would be accepted without proof"; and T5 "Demo: book covers", whose recorded decision record has attention "clean" and exactly one residual item of kind "should", so the page shows "Nothing is accepted without proof". Decision titles and explanations of these demo decisions are free text and are not part of any check. Nothing else of the demo data changes.

interface.ui: Sign-in for the gate preview: GET /auth/preview (redirects to / with an owner session). Decisions page: route /decisions, h1 "Decisions", card header "Open", one list item (role listitem) per open decision. Text matching rule used by every criterion: the "visible text" of an element is its rendered text with surrounding whitespace removed and inner runs of whitespace collapsed to one space; "an element whose whole visible text is X" means some visible element inside the list item (the list item itself or a descendant) has exactly that text. Kind badge: each open-decision list item contains one visible element whose whole visible text is exactly its kind label - "Acceptance", "Contract review", "Confirm on GitHub", "Decision" or "Budget" (unchanged). Identity of an acceptance list item: the list item on /decisions containing a link (role link) whose href is /tasks/{id} (id = decimal digits) and whose whole visible text is "{task key} · {task title}" (e.g. "T4 · Demo: share a list"); in the preview exactly one list item contains such a link per acceptance decision. NEW in each open acceptance list item: (1) exactly one link, to /tasks/{id} of its task, with the visible text "{task key} · {task title}"; (2) one element whose whole visible text is exactly one of "1 item would be accepted without proof", "{n} items would be accepted without proof" (n >= 2, decimal digits) or "Nothing is accepted without proof"; when the acceptance decision has no recorded decision record, neither statement is shown. The acceptance list item contains no button, form, input, select or textarea. Task page: route /tasks/{id}, document title "Task · Agents", h1 whose visible text contains the task key and the task title. Preview demo data (A3): Demo Project task T4 "Demo: share a list" -> "2 items would be accepted without proof"; task T5 "Demo: book covers" -> "Nothing is accepted without proof"; the existing open decisions of T1 (kind badge "Contract review") and T2 (kind badge "Decision") are the only open non-acceptance decisions in the preview.

non_goals: Changing list items of open decisions of any kind other than acceptance on /decisions, the batch card "{n} contracts ready in {project}", or the open-decision strip of the Command page (/).

Listing the individual residual items (their texts, kinds or ids), the basis, blockers, readiness, package hash or decision-record hash on the Decisions page; the task page already lists the residual and keeps doing so unchanged.

Changing how decision records are computed, stored or hashed (decide, ownerSummary, the decision-record artifact, the acceptance decision's recorded context), the evidence package, the gate, the Verifier or the control loop.
Any new button, form, action, filter, sort order or API endpoint (including under /api/v0); approving, rejecting or re-computing anything from the Decisions page.
Changing the database schema or migrations.
Showing the count on the Command page, project pages, the task page or the System page.
Making the Decisions page fit a phone-width screen beyond what it does today.
Adding test-only attributes (such as data-* or ids) to the page for the sake of checking; the checks rely on the visible elements named in the interface.

scope.summary: On the Decisions page (/decisions), in the "Open" card, each open acceptance decision (kind label "Acceptance") additionally shows, read from the decision record recorded for that decision, how many items would be accepted without proof ("{n} items would be accepted without proof", singular "1 item would be accepted without proof"), or "Nothing is accepted without proof" when there are none, and links to its task with a link whose text is the task key and the task title ("{key} · {title}"). The list item stays read-only and shows only recorded facts: nothing is computed beyond counting the recorded residual items, nothing is written, and an acceptance decision without a recorded decision record shows neither statement. Open decisions of other kinds (contract review, confirm on GitHub, decision, budget) are listed as before. The gate preview's demonstration data gains two demo tasks with open acceptance decisions and recorded decision records so the feature can be checked black-box; all earlier demo data stays as it is. Every check identifies a list item by a stable, separately rendered element (the task link by its href and visible text, or the kind badge by its exact text), never by splitting text that mixes the badge, project name, task key and age.
